ballotConstraint.consequence: EVERY elected body in Santa Monica is on the ballot 23 days from this fix, so no new elected-officeholder question was written: per the standing rule, city-tier questions written now buy three weeks. All four additions are APPOINTED officers, whom no election moves (the madison-wi model of distinct offices, never a roll-call).

corrections.text: Who is Santa Monica's City Attorney?
corrections.explanation: Heidi von Tongeln is Santa Monica’s city attorney. The City Council appointed her on March 11, 2026 after a nationwide recruitment; she had served as interim city attorney since September 2025 and as chief deputy city attorney since 2022. Santa Monica’s city attorney is appointed by the Council, not elected.
corrections.wasWrongBecause: Answer was "Douglas Sloan", who resigned as city attorney effective 2025-08-31 — wrong in the live bank for 13 months. The explanation also invented a term: "with a term ending December 1, 2026". Santa Monica’s city attorney is appointed by the Council and has no term.

corrections.text: Ben Allen represents Santa Monica in which chamber of the California Legislature?
corrections.explanation: Ben Allen represents Santa Monica in the California State Senate, the Legislature’s upper chamber. His 24th District runs along the coast of Los Angeles County, from Malibu through Santa Monica to the South Bay. The State Senate has 40 members serving four-year terms.
corrections.wasWrongBecause: Read "Maria Elena Durazo represents Santa Monica in which chamber of the California Legislature?" with the explanation "representing Senate District 26 which includes Santa Monica". Durazo’s SD-26 is central and East Los Angeles. Santa Monica is SD-24, Ben Allen. A false premise, so no option could be right.

additions.text: Who serves as Santa Monica's city manager?
additions.explanation: Oliver Chi became Santa Monica’s city manager in July 2025, selected by the City Council after a nationwide search; he had been Irvine’s city manager since 2021. He succeeded interim city manager Elaine Polachek, who led the city after David White resigned. Under the council-manager charter the city manager runs the departments day to day while the Council sets policy.

additions.text: Darrick Jacob, sworn in during January 2026, leads which Santa Monica city department?
additions.explanation: Darrick Jacob is Santa Monica’s chief of police. City Manager Oliver Chi announced the appointment in December 2025, effective December 14, and Jacob was sworn in on January 14, 2026. He had served with the Santa Monica Police Department since 2004.

additions.text: Which Santa Monica department has Christopher Dishlip directed since April 2026, after serving as its assistant director?
additions.explanation: Christopher Dishlip took over as director of Public Works on April 6, 2026, succeeding Rick Valte, who retired after nearly 26 years with the city. Dishlip had spent nearly 17 years in Santa Monica government, most recently as assistant director of Public Works. Public Works is distinct from SaMoDOT, the separate city transportation department.

additions.text: Who serves as superintendent of the Santa Monica-Malibu Unified School District?
additions.explanation: Antonio M. Shelton, Ed.D., has led the Santa Monica-Malibu Unified School District since July 1, 2023, appointed by its Board of Education after a national search. He had previously been the district’s executive director of secondary schools and principal of Santa Monica High School. The district is governed by its own elected board, separately from the City Council.

Both are the source of the defects above, so the config is corrected in the same change: von Tongeln, and SD-24 Ben Allen.
